questions.question: Describe the contributions of Thomson, Rutherford and Chadwick to our understanding of the atom, and explain what the gold foil experiment showed and how.
questions.expected_answer: Thomson (1897) discovered the electron, a tiny negative particle in all atoms, and proposed the plum pudding model: positive material with electrons scattered through it. Rutherford's team (1909, model 1911) fired fast positive particles at thin gold foil: most passed straight through, so the atom is mostly empty space; a few were deflected through large angles and about 1 in 8 000 bounced back, so the positive charge and almost all the mass are concentrated in a tiny dense nucleus that repels positive particles approaching it head-on. Chadwick (1932) discovered the neutron, a neutral particle in the nucleus with about the same mass as a proton, explaining why nuclei are heavier than their protons alone.

questions.question: Copy and complete a table giving the charge, relative mass and position of the proton, neutron and electron. Explain why an atom is neutral and why nearly all its mass is in the nucleus.
questions.expected_answer: Proton: charge +1, relative mass 1, in the nucleus. Neutron: charge 0, relative mass 1, in the nucleus. Electron: charge −1, relative mass about 1/1836 (negligible), outside the nucleus in shells. An atom is neutral because the number of electrons equals the number of protons, so the charges cancel; neutrons have no charge. Nearly all the mass (more than 99.9%) is in the nucleus because protons and neutrons are each about 1 836 times heavier than an electron, even though the nucleus is only about one hundred-thousandth of the diameter of the atom.

questions.question: For aluminium (atomic number 13, mass number 27) and chlorine (atomic number 17, mass number 35), give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons, and the electron arrangement of each.
questions.expected_answer: Aluminium: 13 protons, 27 − 13 = 14 neutrons, 13 electrons; arrangement 2, 8, 3. Chlorine: 17 protons, 35 − 17 = 18 neutrons, 17 electrons; arrangement 2, 8, 7.
